A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RF-Deep research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original lung-tumor segmentation and OOD detection results, classifier comparisons, ablations, and feature analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds blinded validation, failure analyses, robustness experiments, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: v3 evaluates an enhanced pipeline assigning OOD score 1.0 when segmentation produces no foreground (Section 5.2.3, Table 3). v2 only suggested this possibility and left integration to future work. The standard backbone, hierarchical features, tumor-anchored ROIs, and RF classification procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds two entirely unexposed validation populations: 110 COVID-19-positive chest CTs and 66 institutional breast-cancer CTs, extending evaluation from 2,056 to 2,232 scans. These introduce distinct thoracic disease scenarios. The original datasets remain; MIDRC C19 becoming MIDRC C19− is a clarification.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated MD+ReAct, MD+ASH, and X-Mahalanobis comparisons using the same encoder features and Mahalanobis scoring (Appendix C, Table 8). The original benchmark comparators remain. The deployment-strategy comparison drops Unified and LODO+. KNN and ViM are newly discussed but explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E3.justification: New protocols include ensemble-only blinded validation, acquisition-factor holdouts with thresholds from 0.3 to 0.7, foreground-volume stratification, ROI-restricted logit aggregation, and centered/random crop controls. RF-Deep SHAP analysis switches to the ensemble configuration. These extend the evaluation design; the original segmentation training budget remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of lesion size, absent predictions, acquisition shortcuts, threshold sensitivity, crop anchoring, matched spatial aggregation, and inference cost. SHAP and t-SNE analyses extend to the blinded cohorts. Conversely, the Unified and LODO+ experiments and their generalization analyses are removed.

E5.justification: The 100 matched-seed runs and general 95% bootstrap reporting practice remain. v3 adds Spearman correlations and associated significance tests for foreground volume. It removes v2 Table 6's backbone-specific confidence intervals; the corresponding point estimates remain in v3 Table 12. No increase in repeated-run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 and retained backbone/classifier benchmark values are unchanged. v3 adds blinded AUROCs of 94.71 and 97.32, enhanced-pipeline results, failure rates, acquisition robustness, and timings, while removing Unified/LODO+ results. The new breast-cancer comparison is not uniformly favorable: RF-Radiomics has lower FPR95 than RF-Deep, 7.99 versus 9.78.

T1.justification: The ID/OOD formulation and Appendix B scoring equations are unchanged, as are Appendix A's pretraining descriptions. Added deployment assumptions and empirical explanations introduce no substantive mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central RF-Deep proposal and performance claims remain. v3 more explicitly frames the contribution as a targeted clinical safety filter, qualifies applicability beyond the evaluated Swin backbones, and adds blinded transfer validation as an explicit contribution. Its conclusion also characterizes tumor anchoring as an incremental contribution over strong encoder features.

C2.justification: v3 identifies encoder features as the dominant contributor and anchoring as a refinement, and emphasizes shared ensemble SHAP features rather than dataset-specific activations. It adds substantive discussion of small-lesion failures, Recon 1 false alarms, unaddressed errors within ID scans, unavailable representative outliers, and unvalidated extension to MRI and other backbones.

D1.justification: v3 adds deployment requirements and runtime documentation, including NVIDIA A40 hardware, dual Xeon Platinum 8358 CPUs, CPU classifier inference, and averaging over 50 scans (Table 10). It clarifies consistent RF settings without cohort-specific tuning. Core hyperparameters remain unchanged, while the explicit Recon 1 description of segmentation fine-tuning data is dropped.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for ReAct, ASH, X-Mahalanobis, deep nearest neighbors, ViM, and the COVID-positive dataset. It expands discussion of feature-space alternatives and explains additional baseline exclusions. The broader learner-based versus filter-based positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, several results passages, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. New deployment subsections reorganize the framework narrative, the earlier detailed strategy discussion is condensed, and results are reorganized around transferability and robustness. A new Appendix C shifts the additional-results appendix to D.

P2.justification: v3 adds multiple experimental tables and figures for validation cohorts, foreground volume, crop strategy, and threshold sensitivity. SHAP displays expand from four to six panels, RF-Deep SHAP plots are redrawn for the ensemble, and t-SNE plots include new cohorts. The separate backbone-CI table disappears and the strategy table loses two rows.

improvement.justification: The blinded cohorts, crop/ROI controls, and evaluated absent-prediction extension substantially address v2's gaps in transfer validation, attribution of gains, and handling empty segmentations. New size and acquisition analyses also expose practical failures. These gains outweigh the removed Unified/LODO+ comparisons and backbone confidence intervals, although some broad superiority claims remain stronger than the tables support, including breast-cancer FPR95 in Table 2.
